root_cause_analysis.issue: UTF-16 code unit index vs UTF-8 byte offset divergence in V8 JavaScript runtime
root_cause_analysis.explanation: In JavaScript, string.indexOf() returns UTF-16 character code-unit offsets. Due to multi-byte characters (such as Unicode curly quotes, en-dashes, and mathematical symbols) preceding Section 6 in the raw UTF-8 manuscript, the UTF-16 character position (18332) diverges from the true physical UTF-8 byte offset (18656). Slicing the raw Buffer using character indices produced a 1,904-byte slice with hash 3a2d5c18... rather than the exact 1,918-byte Section 6 body.
root_cause_analysis.resolution: All file buffer operations in R1 repairs explicitly calculate byte offsets via Buffer.byteLength() and slice raw Buffer bytes directly.
